children: shares came under pressure after JPMorgan

cut its price target to $315 from $340, arguing that the software giant still needs to prove its rapidly expanding AI user base can translate into stronger revenue growth. Analyst Arti Vula maintained a Buy rating, however, pointing to Adobe's depressed valuation and potentially significant upside if monetization finally accelerates.

Adobe reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $6.76 billion, up 12.8% from a year earlier and ahead of the $6.69 billion consensus estimate. Adjusted earnings of $6.13 per share also topped expectations of $6.08.

Annual recurring revenue reached $27.5 billion, rising 11.2%, while free cash flow totaled $2.44 billion. Adobe modestly increased its full-year revenue and earnings outlook, although its fourth-quarter revenue forecast came in slightly below Wall Street expectations.

Adobe's AI-first ARR surged 150% to more than $650 million, while Creative freemium monthly active users climbed 70% to over 100 million. Acrobat AI Assistant users doubled sequentially, and ending ARR from the Firefly app and credit packs rose 40% from the previous quarter.

Yet Vula sees a gap between engagement and monetization. Remaining performance obligations increased just 8%, current RPO rose 9%, and Adobe still expects fiscal-2026 net new ARR to decline from last year. The company has also deferred some Creative Cloud pricing actions while prioritizing user acquisition and engagement.
Adobe's investment case increasingly hinges on converting its enormous AI funnel into paying customers.

The most important metrics are AI-first ARR growth, net new ARR, RPO growth and conversion of more than 100 million Creative freemium users into paid subscriptions. Investors should also watch whether Adobe eventually resumes pricing actions without damaging engagement.

JPMorgan's bullish argument rests partly on valuation. Vula estimates Adobe trades at roughly eight times 2027 unlevered free cash flow, leaving a relatively low hurdle for upside if monetization improves. Continued strong engagement without corresponding ARR acceleration, however, could keep pressure on both earnings expectations and the stock's valuation multiple.

title: JPMorgan Resets Adobe Target On Key Reason
